questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes a limited partner in a limited partnership?
options: They manage the business and have unlimited liability.
They are personally liable for every debt the firm incurs.
They do not manage the business, and their liability is limited to their investment.

options: Bondholders receive dividends instead of interest.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of physical capital?

options: Maximizing total revenue regardless of cost
Maximizing the quantity of inputs used

What does the production function Q = f(L, K) describe?
options: The relationship between price and quantity demanded
The maximum output produced from combinations of labour and capital

questions.prompt: A firm can produce 1,000 widgets using any of the following production techniques. Which technique is clearly technically inefficient? Technique A: 25 labour, 50 capital | B: 35 labour, 35 capital C: 50 labour, 25 capital | D: 30 labour, 60 capital
Why does technical efficiency alone not guarantee that a firm is minimizing its costs?
options: Technically efficient methods always produce different outputs.
Different technically efficient methods can have different costs depending on input prices.
Technically efficient methods always use equal quantities of labour and capital.
Technical efficiency requires all factors to have identical prices.

questions.prompt: Using these techniques for producing 1,000 widgets (A: 25 labour, 50 capital; B: 35 labour, 35 capital; C: 50 labour, 25 capital; D: 30 labour, 60 capital), suppose labour and capital each cost $10 per unit. Which technique minimizes total production cost?

Using these techniques for producing 1,000 widgets (A: 25 labour, 50 capital; B: 35 labour, 35 capital; C: 50 labour, 25 capital; D: 30 labour, 60 capital), suppose labour costs $10 per unit and capital costs $5 per unit. Which technique minimizes cost?

Using these techniques for producing 1,000 widgets (A: 25 labour, 50 capital; B: 35 labour, 35 capital; C: 50 labour, 25 capital; D: 30 labour, 60 capital), suppose labour costs $5 per unit and capital costs $10 per unit. Which technique minimizes cost?
A company uses 12 units of labour costing $20 each and 4 units of capital costing $50 each. What is total expenditure on these two inputs?
A firm has MP of labour = 24 and wage = $8; MP of capital = 36 and capital price = $9. At its current input combination, how should it adjust production to reduce cost while maintaining output?
options: Use more labour and less capital.
Keep the existing input combination because costs are minimized.
Use more capital and less labour.
Reduce labour and capital by the same percentage.

questions.prompt: Which condition is necessary for a firm to minimize costs using labour and capital at an interior optimum?
A firm currently has MP_L / p_L = 5 and MP_K / p_K = 2. Which adjustment moves the firm toward cost minimization, assuming it can substitute inputs while maintaining output?
options: Keep the current combination because the ratios are positive.

questions.prompt: Suppose wages rise substantially while the price of capital remains unchanged. According to the principle of substitution, what is a firm likely to do in the long run?
options: Use exactly the same input combination regardless of prices.
Stop attempting to minimize production costs.

questions.prompt: Suppose the price of capital decreases while labour costs remain unchanged. What will a cost-minimizing firm generally do?
options: Substitute relatively more capital for labour.
Substitute relatively more labour for capital.
Reduce the use of capital because it has become cheaper.
Continue with the original input combination regardless of costs.

questions.prompt: A firm has MP_L = 60 and p_L = $20; MP_K = 30 and p_K = $15. What change would move the firm toward cost minimization, assuming it can substitute inputs?
options: Increase both factors by the same amount.
Keep the current combination because marginal products are positive.

questions.prompt: What does the long-run average cost (LRAC) curve represent?
options: Average cost when all production factors are fixed
The lowest possible average cost for each output level when all inputs can vary
The firm's average fixed cost at every output level
The additional cost of producing one more unit

questions.prompt: Why can a short-run average total cost (SRATC) curve never fall below the LRAC curve for the same technology and factor prices?
options: LRAC measures the highest possible production cost.
LRAC represents the lowest attainable cost when all factors can be adjusted.

questions.prompt: What happens where a particular SRATC curve touches the LRAC curve?
options: That plant size is optimal for producing that output level.
The firm must be producing zero output.
The firm's marginal cost must equal zero.
All possible plant sizes necessarily have equal costs.

questions.prompt: A firm needs to produce 100 units per day. Plant SRATC1 has ATC $12; SRATC2 has ATC $9; SRATC3 has ATC $11. Which plant should a cost-minimizing firm choose?
options: All three are equally efficient in cost terms.

questions.prompt: A firm's LRAC curve slopes downward as output increases. What is the firm experiencing?
A firm's LRAC curve rises as output increases. Which concept best explains this?
A firm increases all its inputs by 20%, and output also increases by exactly 20%. What is the firm experiencing?
options: Diminishing marginal product of one fixed input

questions.prompt: A firm doubles all its inputs, and output triples. Which classification applies?
A firm increases all its inputs by 50%, but output increases by only 25%. What does this illustrate?
What is the minimum efficient scale (MES) of a firm?
options: The output where marginal product is zero
The smallest output where LRAC reaches its minimum
The output where total revenue equals total cost
The largest output a firm could physically produce

questions.prompt: A firm has the following LRAC at available outputs: Q=100: $10; Q=200: $8; Q=300: $8; Q=400: $9. What is the smallest output at which it achieves minimum LRAC?
A firm is operating on a SRATC curve that lies above LRAC at its chosen output. What could it do in the long run?
options: Increase its costs to reach LRAC.
Increase fixed costs without changing any inputs.
Adjust its plant size to produce the same output at lower average cost.
Eliminate the relationship between average cost and output.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes production costs in the long run?
options: All factors can vary, so there are no fixed-factor costs in the long-run decision.
Capital costs cannot change when output changes.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes the very long run from the long run?
options: Firms have fewer available production techniques.
At least one factor must remain permanently fixed.
Technology is fixed in the very long run but not in the long run.
Technology itself can change in the very long run.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT one of the three aspects of technological change identified in Chapter 8?
options: Changes in financing interest rates alone

questions.prompt: Why do economists describe technological change as endogenous to the economic system?
options: Firms have incentives to invent and innovate in search of profits.
Technological innovation occurs only because of unpredictable outside events.
Firms have no influence over technological development.
Technology cannot change independently of the size of the labour force.
